items.title: Insilico Medicine advances AI-designed drug Rentosertib for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis into Phase III trials in 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Insilico Medicine has developed Rentosertib, an AI-designed drug targeting TNIK for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a disease currently without a cure. Phase IIa trials showed improved lung function, and Phase III trials with 320 patients are set to begin in 2026. This drug is notable as the first where AI identified both the target and the molecule, marking a significant step in AI-driven drug discovery. While success would represent a treatment rather than a cure, it offers hope for addressing IPF, which currently lacks effective therapies.

items.title: Moat launches $5/month AI membership offering unlimited access to high-quality models at wholesale prices [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Moat introduces a membership plan priced at $5 per month that provides unlimited access to premium AI models at discounted wholesale rates. The service pools usage from a large member base to offer significant cost savings on token usage across various AI models. The membership includes access to models like GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek V4.1 with discounts ranging from 40% to 70% compared to standard prices. Moat offers both monthly and yearly plans, with the yearly plan billed at $60, and claims that the membership can pay for itself with typical usage starting at $9 per month.

items.title: The New York Times advises freelance photographers to avoid updating to Photoshop 2027 due to AI features that may add AI-generated metadata to images [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The New York Times has instructed its freelance photographers not to update to Adobe Photoshop 2027 because the new AI-powered features can embed metadata that identifies photos as AI-generated, which conflicts with the newspaper's policy of minimal photo editing. The email from Times photography leaders highlights concerns that these AI tools, including an AI-assisted editor and image transformation features, may alter images in ways not immediately obvious to users. Adobe has integrated various AI tools into Photoshop and other creative apps, and the 2027 update introduces new AI capabilities accessible from a single toolbar. The Times is cautious about these changes because the metadata tags indicating AI involvement could undermine reader trust, given the paper's commitment to avoiding digital manipulation beyond minimal color adjustments. Adobe began supporting C2PA metadata to track AI edits in August, and the Times' directive aims to prevent such tags from appearing in its published photographs.

items.title: Researchers propose a background-independent algebraic quantization of vacuum general relativity using null cones, deriving finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and recovering black hole entropy corrections
items.content_text: Researchers present a background-independent quantization approach for vacuum general relativity on four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetimes by solving gravitational constraints on intersecting null cones. They construct a nonperturbative Hilbert space representation and define an algebra of observables, enabling a Lorentzian path integral with absolutely convergent sums over intermediate states. The method yields finite closed-form expressions for graviton pair creation and annihilation amplitudes, avoiding divergences seen in perturbative expansions. Using diffeomorphism invariance, the team shows that macroscopic causal diamonds have finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and derives the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy for marginally trapped surfaces, including logarithmic corrections for large Schwarzschild black holes consistent with previous Euclidean results. The approach also recovers the semiclassical Einstein equations at one loop as the low-energy limit of the theory, providing a novel algebraic framework for quantum gravity.

items.title: Software developer warns AI-driven automation may replace specialized coding skills with less skilled labor, threatening long-term software development careers [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A software developer with a background in art and media expresses concern that AI-powered code generation is enabling companies to replace specialized developers with less skilled workers who rely on AI agents. This shift, driven by automation and the use of large language models, is reducing the demand for deep expertise in software development, particularly in areas like front-end and server-side coding. The developer highlights examples where teams use AI to generate code across different specializations without understanding the underlying technologies, leading to lower quality and less reliable software. Despite initial productivity claims, this trend risks devaluing skilled labor and lowering wages in the software industry over time. The article suggests that while AI tools may not fully replace developers immediately, they are already reshaping the profession and could undermine career prospects in the long term.

items.title: Dev-Mem launches local-first SQLite knowledge graph to preserve development context for AI coding agents across sessions [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Dev-Mem is a persistent local knowledge store designed for AI coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and OpenCode. It records decisions, failed approaches, constraints, and discoveries during coding sessions and injects relevant information into new sessions to avoid repeated mistakes, all while keeping data on the user's machine without server dependencies beyond existing LLM API keys. The tool requires Node.js 22+ and an existing project with agent directories or a Claude Code project. It supports multiple LLM API keys including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini, and can be installed globally via npm. Dev-Mem automatically detects agent directories, installs hooks, and manages a local .dev-mem directory for storing knowledge graphs, which is gitignored by default. It offers CLI commands for status checks, diagnostics, uninstalling hooks, and wrapping commands to ensure data extraction on session end, particularly useful for agents lacking reliable session events.

items.title: Google marks 15 years in Colombia with over $1 million Google.org investment in AI education, small businesses, rural youth, and disaster relief [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Google is celebrating 15 years of operations in Colombia by investing more than $1 million through Google.org to support initiatives in AI education, small business training, rural youth development, and disaster relief efforts. The company highlights its growth from a small local team to a significant presence introducing tools like Android Earthquake Alerts and Google Wallet, while promoting local culture through projects such as Google Street View. The funding supports programs including AI teacher training with Fundación Pies Descalzos, small business AI literacy led by CENIA and Fundación Futuro del Trabajo, rural youth training via Colnodo's JuvenTIC program, and humanitarian aid for communities affected by recent earthquakes. Google emphasizes the importance of investing in Colombia's talent to unlock economic opportunities from AI adoption, citing reports that project billions in potential annual economic gains.

The workspace supports users in managing financial tasks more efficiently by integrating AI capabilities with sustained contextual awareness.

items.title: Study finds junior developers gain the most productivity boost from AI tools, accelerating learning and narrowing experience gaps with seniors [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A recent analysis challenges the notion that AI primarily benefits senior developers by showing that junior developers gain significant advantages from AI assistance, accelerating their learning curve and improving problem-solving skills. Experienced engineers leverage AI to enhance productivity based on their prior knowledge, but juniors benefit by quickly acquiring insights that traditionally required years of experience. Research from MIT and Stanford involving over 5,000 workers found that less experienced developers resolved tasks up to 34% faster with generative AI, absorbing patterns from top performers. This shift is influencing hiring practices, with companies like Anthropic focusing less on coding interviews and more on judgment and ideas, reflecting AI's role in leveling the playing field between juniors and seniors in software development.

items.title: VAAS-X launches persistent memory platform for AI agents and machines to record and recall outcomes across multiple systems [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: VAAS-X offers a persistent memory solution for AI agents and machines, enabling them to record experiences, actions, and outcomes for improved recall and decision-making. The platform supports integration with agents like Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor via a connector, as well as SDKs for code and device data streams, all managed through a unified interface. The system provides fast, on-device memory search without per-query charges, running on existing hardware from microcontrollers to enterprise servers. It prioritizes successful outcomes in recall and maintains a full audit trail for stored memories. Security features include encryption in transit and at rest, with plans for encrypted-data operation to enhance compliance for enterprise deployments.

items.title: Italy and Switzerland warn of autonomous AI-driven cyberattacks targeting critical infrastructure with rapid, coordinated AI agents exploiting vulnerabilities [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: Italian and Swiss cybersecurity agencies have issued warnings about autonomous AI-driven cyberattacks targeting organizations in critical infrastructure sectors. These attacks involve AI agents that identify and exploit vulnerabilities and misconfigurations on exposed systems, sometimes operating in parallel to compromise large numbers of endpoints within hours. Italy's CSIRT reported campaigns where AI agents chained vulnerabilities and wrote malicious code in real time to evade defenses and penetrate internal networks. Switzerland's National Cyber Security Center confirmed the first successful AI-assisted breaches, noting a rise in publicly available AI attack tools and recommending rapid patching, multi-factor authentication, and least-privilege access to mitigate risks.

items.title: Study finds firms with higher use of task-specific AI agents predict slower hiring growth over six to nine months [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A recent study analyzing data from over 400 AI models and 34.8 million U.S. job postings finds that firms with greater exposure to agentic AI-AI agents designed for specific tasks-experience a 2.11% to 3.20% slower growth in job postings over six to nine months. This effect is more pronounced following the release of advanced AI agents like Claude Code 2.0 and is concentrated in non-senior job roles, with no significant impact on senior positions or broad AI usage. The research combines proprietary AI consumption data with firm-level stock return analysis to measure exposure to agentic AI and validates findings using firms' mentions of AI deployment in securities filings and earnings calls. The results suggest that the adoption of specialized AI agents may influence labor demand differently than general AI technologies, potentially slowing workforce expansion in certain job categories.

items.title: Stanford physicist uses AI to address challenges in quantum gravity research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A physicist at Stanford University has applied artificial intelligence techniques to tackle problems in quantum gravity, aiming to advance the understanding of fundamental physics. This approach seeks to overcome longstanding theoretical difficulties by leveraging AI's computational capabilities. The work represents an intersection of cutting-edge physics and machine learning, potentially opening new avenues for research in quantum gravity.

items.title: Lintsure applies rule-based checker to 561 public projects, finds 25% have clear code problems, with payment-related projects most affected [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Lintsure ran its rule-based static analysis tool on 561 public software projects, mostly developed with AI coding tools, covering 51 million lines of code. The analysis found that 25% of projects had at least one clear problem, and 21% had a high-severity issue, with projects handling payments or sign-in features showing significantly higher problem rates. The checker flagged issues such as personal data logged in plaintext, unsafe container configurations, and unfixed dependency versions. The study revealed that the nature of a project influenced the likelihood of problems more than whether AI was involved in its development. Larger projects and those serving users over a network tended to have more findings. Additionally, most projects lacked basic security housekeeping like software bill of materials (SBOM) and automatic dependency updates. The tool's findings were validated with an 80% accuracy rate on reviewed samples, highlighting common security and quality concerns in AI-assisted codebases.

items.title: Jack Despain Zhou says AI causes de-individualization by making content indistinguishable across platforms, citing frequent presence of Claude in media and communications [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Jack Despain Zhou highlights the de-individualization effect of AI, noting that AI-generated content, particularly from Claude, pervades various media such as YouTube videos, conference presentations, and emails. This widespread presence blurs individual authorship and reputation, as serious credentials and institutions are associated with AI-generated outputs. Zhou's observation reflects concerns about the homogenization of content and the challenge of distinguishing human-generated work from AI-generated material, raising questions about authenticity and personal identity in digital communications.

items.title: Analysis: AI regulation cannot follow the model used for oil due to fundamental differences in technology and impact [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The article argues that artificial intelligence should not be regulated using frameworks designed for commodities like oil, as AI's nature and societal effects differ significantly. It explores the challenges in understanding AI's complexities and the pitfalls of applying traditional regulatory approaches to this rapidly evolving technology. The discussion highlights the need for new regulatory paradigms tailored to AI's unique characteristics and potential risks.

items.title: Anthropic completes $81.3 billion IPO as Grand Theft Auto VI launches with record $3.79 billion day one sales, highlighting contrasting approaches to AI and creative production [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Anthropic went public with an $81.3 billion IPO on the same day that Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto VI, which earned $3.79 billion on its first day and became the highest-rated game on Metacritic. GTA VI was developed over 13 years by about 5,000 people without using generative AI, emphasizing handcrafted detail and complexity. The simultaneous events underscore a contrast between the AI industry's focus on efficiency and automation, exemplified by Anthropic, and the traditional, labor-intensive creative process behind GTA VI. Industry leaders debate the future of game development as AI tools like Google's Project Genie emerge, but GTA VI's success suggests that deeply crafted, human-driven entertainment remains highly valued.

items.title: Proposal for Open Knowledge Models as an alternative to open-weight and closed AI models to improve transparency and control [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Open Knowledge Models are proposed as a new approach to AI that separates cognitive processing from knowledge storage, unlike current open-weight or closed models that embed knowledge directly into model weights. This separation aims to enhance transparency, explainability, and human control by maintaining external databases for knowledge while keeping the model's cognitive core small and understandable. The concept, supported by some international academic research, addresses concerns about data provenance and intellectual property by allowing proprietary and public data to coexist distinctly. It also extends to software development through a layered programming pipeline that enables human experts to monitor and understand AI-generated code. Advocates suggest government investment in these models to ensure AI remains comprehensible and controllable, emphasizing that this approach supports commerce and is not anti-capitalist.

items.title: OpenAI fixes GPT-6.2 Astra pricing bug causing users to hit limits 40% faster, offers extra resets and free Fast Mode for business subscribers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI corrected a billing error that had given GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol users incorrect discounts, resulting in Astra users hitting usage limits 40% faster and Sol users 25% faster than the previous week. The company will not retroactively charge for the discrepancy and has provided all Go, Plus, Pro, and Business subscribers with an extra reset, while business users receive free Fast Mode access through the end of the year. The pricing bug affected only GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models, with other models unaffected. OpenAI is also experimenting with merging Chat and Work modes for select Pro users, combining direct responses with agentic workflows in a single cloud environment to enhance capabilities despite higher token costs.

items.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
items.content_text: My comment on The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features - Hacker News. I had a NYT photographer take my picture at my home earlier this year (for a story about Moltbook, oddly enough). At one point I asked if they could fix things up if I had a stain on my shirt and they said absolutely not - they present photographs as they were taken, with cropping and balancing applied but no edits beyond that. He did spend a bunch of time trying to find the best possible natural lighting for the shots he wanted. The photo at the top of https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/02/technology/moltbook-ai-so... is my laptop, taken in my garden, after hunting around for the best spot that didn't have too much glare on the screen. You can see how dirty my screen is, too! Photography for a newspaper is photo journalism, and they take it seriously. (Thankfully I did not have a visible stain on my shirt.) Tags: photography, new-york-times, hacker-news, journalism

items.title: DoorDash Scales Dispatch 10x While Maintaining 99.99% Peak Availability [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: DoorDash has redesigned its real-time dispatch platform, replacing a monolithic optimization engine with a distributed architecture that separates coordination from computation. The new system delivers 10x higher throughput and more than 99.99% peak availability. It also supports hybrid machine learning inference and multi-agent reinforcement learning to dynamically optimize delivery assignments. By Leela Kumili
